dissents.topic: Severity of missing `import sys` in the two mathimpl.py files

positions.position: P0 — NameError at import time on every Python version; author has not verified the invariant 'sys is in scope here.'
P0 — patch was not actually run; will break `import numba` on a fresh 3.11 interpreter.
P0 — textbook unestablished precondition; defect any test execution would expose immediately.
P1 — flagged as a likely failure but framed as 'verify both files import sys'; treats it as incidental complexity from the version-check approach rather than a confirmed defect.
P1 — SPEC-MISSING / likely NameError on 3.11+, but contingent on whether sys is already imported.
P1 — will raise NameError on every Python version if sys isn't already imported; recommends using PYVERSION instead.

dissents.topic: Severity of the indentation/blank-line issue around the Math_unary registration in mathdecl.py

positions.position: P0 — literate-programming failure and source-layout off-by-one that will trip future contributors.
P0 — indentation/whitespace sloppiness that breaks the file's voice; conditional is glued to the class.
P0 — structurally broken placement; missing blank line invites accidentally pulling the if into the class body on future edits.
P1 — the real issue is rebinding the module-level name `Math_unary`, complecting template definition with registration; fix by dropping the assignment.
P1 — fragile name-rebinding could silently break if infer_global ever returns a wrapper; placement is misleading.
P1 — parses fine but reads ambiguously; restore the blank line.

dissents.topic: How to unify the Python 3.11 version gate

positions.position: Use `hasattr(math, 'exp2')` once as a named predicate — the actual question is symbol existence, not Python version; needs no new import.
Use the project's existing `PYVERSION` constant everywhere; project has chosen it as single source of truth.
Either delete all guards (if numba already requires >=3.11) or route through `PYVERSION` centrally; pick one — current mix of sys.version_info and PYVERSION is BAD-TASTE.
Unify on `PYVERSION` across all four sites; the test already uses it.
Use `PYVERSION` — version-gate the data, not the code; data dominates.
Express the predicate once (PYVERSION) and iterate over a declared list of intrinsics; current scattered ifs are 'gotos disguised as conditionals.'

issues.description: Missing `import sys` in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py while both reference `sys.version_info`
issues.detail: Both impl files newly use `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` but the diff does not show an `import sys` being added to either. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, this is an immediate NameError at import time — meaning `import numba` itself breaks on the very Python versions the guard is meant to enable. Knuth, Torvalds, and Dijkstra rate this P0 (outright defect, author did not run the modified code); Hickey, Liskov, and Pike rate this P1 contingent on whether `sys` is already imported in those files.

issues.description: Indentation / blank-line collapse around the Math_unary version-gated registration in mathdecl.py
issues.detail: The blank line separating the `Math_unary` class body from the next decorator was removed; `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11): Math_unary = infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` now sits at module scope but visually glued to the class. This is a literate-programming / source-layout failure (Knuth), a BAD-TASTE whitespace violation (Torvalds), and a structural defect that invites future edits to pull the `if` into the class body (Dijkstra). Hickey and Liskov additionally flag that rebinding the module-level name `Math_unary` to `infer_global(...)(Math_unary)` complects template definition with side-effecting registration and is fragile if `infer_global` ever returns a wrapper.

issues.description: Version-gate inconsistency: production code uses `sys.version_info` while the test file uses `PYVERSION` from numba.core.utils
issues.detail: The same fact ('math.exp2 exists on Python >= 3.11') is expressed four times across four files using two different mechanisms. The project already exposes `numba.core.utils.PYVERSION` as the canonical version predicate and the test imports it; production code should do the same. Hickey goes further and recommends `hasattr(math, 'exp2')` as the most honest predicate — symbol existence is the actual question. Dijkstra calls this a 'smuggled goto': control jumps over a registration in each module independently with no single source of truth.

issues.description: No correctness reasoning that llvm.exp2 matches CPython math.exp2 across all input types and edge cases
issues.detail: The patch binds math.exp2 to the LLVM `llvm.exp2` intrinsic with no argument that the two are semantically equivalent across int8..uint64, float32, float64, including +/-inf, NaN, subnormals, overflow, underflow, and the uint64-near-2^63 conversion path. Dijkstra: 'testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence.' Liskov frames the same gap in LSP terms: the substitution contract (njit'd exp2 behaves the same as CPython math.exp2) is not exercised at boundary values.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline (per-reviewer severity varies)
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends with `\ No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files end with a newline; most lint/CI tools flag this. Torvalds rates it P1 ('the diff literally announces it'); Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike, and Dijkstra rate it P2. Preserved at the higher severity per the no-averaging rule.

issues.description: No literate comment explains why exp2 is version-gated
issues.detail: Each `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` site lacks a one-line comment noting that `math.exp2` was added to the Python stdlib in 3.11. A future reader has to look this up. Knuth's canonical literate-programming nit.

issues.description: Test x_values are a copy-paste of test_exp and do not exercise exp2-distinguishing behavior
issues.detail: `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` was cloned from `test_exp`. For exp2 specifically, inputs like 0, 1, 2, 10 produce exact integer results (2^x) and would catch a wrong-intrinsic regression (e.g., accidental wiring to `llvm.exp`). The current test would not catch that bug by design — only by coincidence. Pike, Hickey, Torvalds, Liskov, and Dijkstra all flag this; Knuth separately notes that feeding negative values through uint types relies on an unstated wraparound + inf==inf invariant.
`[-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` repeats -2 and 2, reducing the distinct-input count. Harmless but a copy-paste artifact from test_exp; reveals that the test was cloned without thought.

issues.description: Release note body is content-free / restates the title
issues.detail: The body `Support for math.exp2 is added.` repeats the title `Add support for math.exp2.` and adds no information. Should at minimum mention the Python 3.11+ requirement, and ideally that the implementation routes to `llvm.exp2`.

issues.description: Supported-functions docs entry does not note Python 3.11+ minimum
issues.detail: `docs/source/reference/pysupported.rst` lists `math.exp2` alongside `math.exp` with no qualifier, but the implementation is conditional on Python >= 3.11. A short parenthetical would prevent a 3.10 user from filing a bug.

issues.description: Duplicate conditional-registration pattern across three files invites future drift
issues.detail: The same `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` + `'llvm.exp2'` pattern appears in mathdecl.py, cpython/mathimpl.py, and np/math/mathimpl.py. Manageable for one function; for the next several 3.11+ math additions it becomes a maintenance liability. The contract for 'a unary math function added in 3.11 that maps to an LLVM intrinsic' could be declared once.

issues.description: Test integer-type cases rely on unstated wraparound + inf==inf invariant for uint types
issues.detail: Math_unary's `cases` list includes int8..int64 and uint8..uint64, but the test feeds values like `-2` through uint16/uint32/uint64. The assertion presumably passes because -2 becomes (2^N - 2), math.exp2 of which overflows to inf in both CPython and the compiled path, so the comparison is inf == inf. If that is the intended invariant it should be written down; if not, the test is asserting an accident.

issues.description: LLVM lowering complexity/accuracy story is unstated
issues.detail: `unary_math_intr(math.exp2, 'llvm.exp2')` delegates to LLVM's exp2 intrinsic with accuracy and complexity inherited from libm-style intrinsics. Worth one sentence in the PR description noting that exp2 follows the same lowering pattern as exp/log2/log10. A literate-programming note, not a code change.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converged on the same two highest-severity issues: (1) the two mathimpl.py files reference `sys.version_info` without `import sys` shown in the diff — Knuth, Torvalds, and Dijkstra rate this P0 (NameError at import on the very Python versions the guard is meant to enable; clear evidence the patch was not run), while Hickey, Liskov, and Pike rate it P1 contingent on whether `sys` is already imported; and (2) the blank-line collapse in mathdecl.py glues a module-scope `if` to the `Math_unary` class body, with Hickey and Liskov adding that rebinding the class name via `infer_global(math.exp2)(Math_unary)` complects definition with side-effecting registration. All six also flag the version-gate inconsistency between `sys.version_info` (production) and `PYVERSION` (test) as needing unification — though Hickey dissents on the unification target, arguing for `hasattr(math, 'exp2')` over PYVERSION because symbol existence is the actual question. The strongest preserved disagreement is on severity of the missing `import sys`: it is either a confirmed P0 defect or a P1 'verify this' concern depending on the reviewer's willingness to assume the import is already present. Dijkstra and Liskov uniquely push for stronger correctness reasoning (edge cases: inf/NaN/overflow/underflow/large-int conversion) on top of the structural fixes.
